name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell for execution of commands and scripts.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: Adversaries abuse the Windows command shell (cmd.exe) for execution.

name: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: Adversaries abuse WMI to execute malicious commands and payloads.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Adversaries abuse task scheduling to execute code, often for persistence.

name: Scheduled Task
description: Adversaries abuse the Windows Task Scheduler to run programs on a schedule.

name: System Services
description: Adversaries abuse system services or daemons to execute commands or programs.

name: User Execution
description: Adversaries rely on a user opening a malicious file or link to gain execution.

name: Native API
description: Adversaries interact directly with the native OS API to execute behaviors.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
description: Adversaries configure system settings to automatically execute a program at boot or logon.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
description: Adversaries add programs to Registry run keys or the startup folder to persist.

name: Create or Modify System Process
description: Adversaries create or modify system-level processes to repeatedly execute payloads.

name: Windows Service
description: Adversaries create or modify Windows services to execute malicious payloads.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries create accounts to maintain access to victim systems.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adversaries manipulate accounts to maintain or elevate access to systems.

name: Web Shell
description: Adversaries plant web shells on servers to maintain persistent remote access.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries bypass elevation control mechanisms to obtain higher privileges.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate privileges.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries inject code into processes to evade defenses and elevate privileges.

name: Indicator Removal
description: Adversaries delete or modify artifacts to remove evidence of their activity.

name: File Deletion
description: Adversaries delete files they create or use to remove traces of intrusion.

name: Modify Registry
description: Adversaries modify the Windows Registry to evade defenses or hide configuration.

name: Impair Defenses
description: Adversaries disable or modify security tools and logging to avoid detection.

name: Disable or Modify Tools
description: Adversaries disable or tamper with security software to avoid detection.

name: Masquerading
description: Adversaries manipulate names or locations of objects to appear legitimate.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution
description: Adversaries bypass controls by proxying execution through trusted system binaries.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries obfuscate files or content to hinder analysis and detection.

name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
description: Adversaries decode or deobfuscate payloads to make them usable at runtime.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries dump credentials from the operating system and software.

name: LSASS Memory
description: Adversaries extract credential material from LSASS process memory.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries guess or crack passwords to gain access to accounts.

name: Credentials from Password Stores
description: Adversaries harvest credentials from password managers and stores.

name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
description: Adversaries steal or forge Kerberos tickets to authenticate as other users.

name: Unsecured Credentials
description: Adversaries search for credentials stored insecurely across a system.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Adversaries gather detailed information about the operating system and hardware.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate files and directories to locate information of interest.

name: Process Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate running processes on a system.

name: Remote System Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate other systems on the network by IP, hostname, or service.

name: System Network Configuration Discovery
description: Adversaries gather details about the network configuration of a system.

name: Account Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate accounts on a system or in a domain.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries use valid accounts over remote services to move laterally.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries use RDP with valid credentials to move laterally between systems.

name: Lateral Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools between systems within a compromised environment.

name: Data from Local System
description: Adversaries collect data from the local system prior to exfiltration.

name: Archive Collected Data
description: Adversaries compress or encrypt collected data before exfiltration.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries communicate using application layer protocols to blend with traffic.

name: Web Protocols
description: Adversaries use HTTP/S protocols for command and control to blend with web traffic.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools or files from an external system into the environment.

name: Encrypted Channel
description: Adversaries use encryption to conceal command and control traffic.

name: Proxy
description: Adversaries use a proxy to route and obscure command and control traffic.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing C2 channel.

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
description: Adversaries exfiltrate data to a legitimate external web service.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability (ransomware).

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Adversaries delete or disable recovery features to prevent system restoration.

name: Service Stop
description: Adversaries stop or disable services to render systems unusable.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries use legitimate credentials to gain and maintain access.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit internet-facing applications to gain initial access.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Adversaries send targeted emails with malicious attachments to gain access.
